blocks.text: This chapter reports what the Shaddad digital twin demonstrated in Phase 1, in which an operator drives the robot through the simulated SBUS remote-control link. It covers the nine Phase 1 acceptance scenarios (S0, S1, S2, S6a to S6d, S8a and S8b) and the free demonstration drive D1 of `phase1_test_drive`. All scenario and D1 results are from 2026-10-23, after the fix pass described in `docs/STATUS.md` section 0, and all were simulated in Normal mode; the unit-test regression reported at the end of the chapter predates the fix pass. The criteria values come from `docs/report/results_phase1.json`, which was written from the saved result files in `work/results/`. The one exception is the S1 residual eps_el, which the JSON rounds to 0; it is given unrounded from the saved S1 result file.

**Overall result: 64 of 71 criteria PASS, 6 FAIL, 1 BLOCKED.** S0, S6c, S6d and S8a pass every criterion, and S1 passes all 12 criteria that could be evaluated. The six failures are margin violations (short deceleration overshoots in S6a and S6b, a 0.9 % high mean deceleration in S8b, and the slope case S2), not functional failures. In every scenario the robot powered up correctly and stopped when it had to; where the scenario tests it, the robot moved again only after the required re-arm (S6a, S6b) or reset and re-arm (S8a).
Test method
How a scenario run works
Each scenario is a MATLAB function in `scripts/scenarios/` that returns a `Simulink.SimulationInput` for `Shaddad_System` and a list of pass/fail criteria. `run_scenario` executes it in five steps:

items: `run_scenario('S6b')` splits the id into the scenario `S6` and the variant letter `b` and calls `scn_S6_rc_failsafe(P, 'Variant', 'b')`.

The scenario function builds the operator input with `scn_rc_tab` (transmitter on at 0.5 s, arm switch on at 2 s, sticks neutral) and `scn_rc_stick` (stick positions that the MCU decodes as exactly the target speed). Variant controls go into the `SimulationInput`, not the base workspace.
`sim` runs the full Phase 1 chain from `RC_Link_Sim` through `Shaddad_MCU` and CAN to the drives and tracks in `Shaddad_Plant`, with `Shaddad_BMS` managing the pack.
`scn_collect` gathers the logged signals into a struct `S`, and `eval_criteria(S, crit)` computes each criterion's metric and compares it with its limit.

The result (criteria, collected logs, KPIs, wall time, RTF) is saved as `work/results/<id>_<yyyymmdd_HHMMSS>.mat`. `scn_reeval(id)` re-evaluates the latest saved file with the current criteria code without simulating again.

blocks.text: **Real-time factor.** In this chapter RTF is the simulated time divided by the execution wall time (`SimulationMetadata.TimingInfo.ExecutionElapsedWallTime`), so the model compile is excluded. The wall time quoted next to it includes compile and initialisation.
Where the criteria come from

The criteria are based on `docs/architecture.md` section 12. The scenario scripts add preconditions (speed or position before the event), restart checks, a reverse-speed and a collision check in S1, energy-audit and pitch criteria (T-INT-08, T-INT-04), the ESTOP entry time of S8b and the S6d variant. They also switch the S1 transmitter on at 0.5 s instead of 2 s and insert the S1 throttle release from 1.2 m/s ({tab:tab_s1_sched}). Most limits are not free choices. They follow from binding design decisions, whose replay calculations give the expected value; the limit adds a margin to it ({tab:tab_crit_origin}).

blocks.text: Meaning of PASS, FAIL and BLOCKED

`eval_criteria` gives every criterion one of the four status values PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED and ERROR defined in {tab:tab_status} ({sec:ch08_user_manual/Reading the criteria table}). `run_scenario` derives the scenario verdict from them: `res.pass` is true when the simulation ended without error and every criterion is PASS or BLOCKED, and `tests/system/tScenarios.m` applies the same rule.
In the totals of this chapter a BLOCKED criterion is counted separately and never as a pass. A scenario is called PASS only when every criterion that could be evaluated passed.
Provenance of the results

All results were produced on 2026-10-23 after the fix pass: the torque-availability deadlock in `drive_esc/Torque_Limiter` (`build_drive.m`, `tau_avail = min(TauThMot, TauDcm)`), the `drive_ready` wiring in `build_shaddad_mcu.m`, the SBUS frame rejection in `subsystems/electronics/sbus_frame_sync.m` and the ESC undervoltage latch. D1, S0, S2, S6a, S6b and S8b were simulated again for this report between 20:11 and 20:47. S1, S6c, S6d and S8a reuse the post-fix runs of 07:25 to 07:56; the later fixes of the same day address the HW (`VC_TARGET` 1) variants (STATUS section 0). MATLAB was restarted between runs, because MATLAB memory grows with every full-system compile ({sec:ch08_user_manual/PC requirements}). The runs can be repeated with one scenario per MATLAB session:

openProject('<project root>\Shaddad_UGV.prj');
% one run per MATLAB session: restart MATLAB and reopen the project before the next line
r0 = run_scenario('S0');                         % 10 s power-up
r1 = run_scenario('S1', 'Mode', 'normal');       % 120 s RC drive
r  = run_scenario('S2');                         % likewise 'S6a', 'S6b', 'S6c', 'S6d', 'S8a', 'S8b'
res = phase1_test_drive('Replay', false);       % D1 demonstration drive
shaddad_replay_birdseye(res.file);               % bird's-eye replay of a saved run
r = scn_reeval('S8a', 'Save', false);            % re-evaluate the latest saved S8a result

Power-up and safety re-arm (S0)

S0 (`scn_S0_smoke.m`) runs 10 s with all inputs zero: key on, transmitter off, flat test field. It checks the normative power-up sequence of ICD 6 (D30). The MCU boots and drives DO0 (MCU_SAFETY_OK) high, then sends one automatic 50 ms DO1 SAFETY_RESET_REQ pulse. The safety relay closes its immediate contacts (Safety_OK, STO released) and delayed contacts (Safety_HV_OK, K1/K2 coil supply). The BMS then precharges and closes the contactors (HV_Ready), and the MCU completes its self-test and enters STANDBY. The robot must not move and the SOC must not change. {tab:tab_s0_crit} lists the criteria and the results.

blocks.caption: S0 criteria (re-run 2026-10-23 20:47)
rows: No NaN or Inf in truth, power truth and KPIs

blocks.caption: S0 power-up timeline (re-run 2026-10-23 20:47): DO0 MCU_SAFETY_OK, the 50 ms DO1 re-arm pulse, Safety_OK and Safety_HV_OK, BMS HV_Ready and the MCU mode BOOT -> SELFTEST -> STANDBY.

blocks.text: {fig:F25_s0_powerup.png} shows the sequence. DO0 rises at 20 ms. The DO1 pulse runs from 40 to 90 ms, because D30 starts it only after DO0 has been high for 20 ms. The relay contacts close at 61 ms, 21 ms after the pulse starts. HV_Ready follows at 0.5 s with the 4.7 Ω precharge override, and STANDBY at 1.01 s, after the 1.0 s self-test (`P.electronics.safety.selftest_t`). The MCU stays in STANDBY, because the transmitter is off and the robot is never armed. The acceptance run before the fix pass gave the same 11/11 result, so the fix pass did not change the power-up behaviour.
RC driving (S1)

S1 (`scn_S1_rc_drive.m`) is the main Phase 1 acceptance drive: 120 s on the flat test field without an implement. {tab:tab_s1_sched} lists the operator inputs and {tab:tab_s1_crit} the criteria and results.

blocks.caption: S1 RC drive (post-fix run 2026-10-23 07:25): forward speed and yaw rate against the MCU command and the shaped reference over 120 s, with the start to 1.2 m/s, the right turn from 30 to 45 s, the throttle release at 52 s (stop-distance segment) and the reverse drive at -0.6 m/s.

blocks.text: {fig:F26_s1_response.png} shows the response. The speed reaches 90 % of 1.2 m/s after 1.51 s and settles 0.6 % below the target without overshoot, because the MCU shaper ramps the reference and the ESC speed loop (D50 gains) follows it. In the right turn the yaw rate stays within 4.9 % of the MCU reference, with the sign convention of D18 (steering right gives a negative, clockwise yaw rate). After the throttle release the robot stops in 0.844 m, a little shorter than the 0.88 m of the D33 replay. The energy audit closes to machine precision on the electrical side and to 4.4e-5 on the mechanical side, so the plant networks neither create nor lose energy.

blocks.caption: S1 latency evidence at the 5 s throttle step: transmitter frame, decoded SBUS channel, DRV_CMD speed reference and ESC speed reference. TX frame -> DRV_CMD 28 ms (limit 30 ms), stick -> ESC reference 50 ms (limit 65 ms).

blocks.text: {fig:F27_s1_latency.png} breaks the latency down at the 5 s throttle step. From the transmitter frame emission, one 14 ms radio frame, about 4 ms of SBUS bytes and decoder poll, and up to 10 ms of Task_10 phase give 28 ms to the DRV_CMD frame. This is the upper end of the D37 budget (18-28 ms) and leaves 2 ms to the 30 ms limit. From the operator stick, a further 12 ms (10 ms input rate transition plus the phase to the next transmitter frame) and the 10 ms ESC rate transition give 50 ms, inside the 38-62 ms budget.

**S1 before and after the fix pass.** With the files delivered to the acceptance run, S1 failed: the latencies passed, but the robot never moved, because the MCU torque limit and the ESC torque availability held each other at 0 N m (STATUS section 6, item 1). The fix in `build_drive.m` removed this zero fixed point. The post-fix run gives practically the same criteria values as the in-memory probe of the acceptance run (for example a stop distance of 0.844 m against 0.845 m).

**Why S1.rtf is BLOCKED.** The RTF ≥ 5 target of D56 applies to Accelerator mode with the top model and every Model block compiled. During the acceptance run Accelerator mode still worked: a 20 s S1 with only the top model in Accelerator reached RTF 1.07 (STATUS section 5.2). After the acceptance, Windows Application Control on the reference PC blocks the MEX files that Accelerator and Rapid Accelerator generate (STATUS section 0), so every run of this chapter uses Normal mode (measured S1 RTF 0.47). The blocked text in `scn_S1_rc_drive.m` still gives the older reason 'no C compiler', although the MinGW64 14.2 compiler is installed (STATUS open problem 15). The full target has never been measured.
Demonstration drive (D1)

D1 is the default test drive of `phase1_test_drive` and the recommended first run for a new user (see {sec:ch08_user_manual/Running the Phase 1 test drive}). It has no pass/fail criteria: `scn_D1_test_drive` converts a plan of [t v w] rows into transmitter stick positions and returns an empty criteria list. The run reported here is `phase1_test_drive('Replay', false)` of 2026-10-23 20:11 (`work/results/D1_20261023_201131.mat`): 64 s simulated in 146 s of execution and 251 s of wall time, RTF 0.44. {fig:F23_d1_dashboard.png} in {sec:ch08_user_manual/Reading the figure} shows the summary figure that `phase1_test_drive` draws at the end of the run, {fig:F24_d1_birdseye.png} the final frame of the replay, and {tab:tab_d1_track} compares the plan, the targets decoded by the MCU and the true motion in each segment. The values are means over the last part of each segment, after the transient (for example 9 to 13.95 s for the first straight).

blocks.caption: D1 command tracking per plan segment: v in m/s, w (yaw rate) in rad/s, + = left

items: **Mode sequence.** BOOT at 0 s, SELFTEST at 0.01 s, STANDBY at 1.01 s and MANUAL at 2.04 s, 40 ms after the arm edge. The MCU stays in MANUAL until the end.
**Command decoding.** The MCU targets equal the plan within 0.0013 m/s and 0.0006 rad/s, so the stick conversion and the MCU RC mapping agree end to end.

**Speed tracking.** On the straights and in reverse the true speed is within 0.007 m/s of the MCU target. In the arcs it is lower: 0.782 m/s for 0.8 m/s and 0.476 m/s for 0.5 m/s. This is consistent with the track slip in the turns ({fig:F31_drive_internals.png}), because the MCU controls the track belt speed, not the ground speed.
**Yaw tracking.** The yaw rate follows the target within about 0.011 rad/s in every segment. The maximum, 0.553 rad/s, is a short transient in the 0.5 rad/s pivot turn.
**Link and safety.** 4571 SBUS frames accepted, 0 rejected, no link loss after arming, 0 collisions. The MCU motor torque limit stayed at the full 16 N m, so the MCU never derated the drive.
**Path.** 34.8 m driven at up to 1.192 m/s; the robot ends at x = -1.28 m, y = 7.64 m.

blocks.text: The |e_pos| = 7.75 m field in the title of {fig:F24_d1_birdseye.png} compares the true position with the navigation estimate. Phase 1 computes no navigation estimate (`GNC_Stub`), so this value has no meaning here.
Battery and drive internals during D1

The drive takes 10.33 Wh from the pack, about 0.58 kW on average over 64 s including the standby loads. The true SOC falls from 95.854 % to 95.789 %, the pack current peaks at 25.5 A and the terminal voltage stays between 53.5 V and 53.7 V. The cell temperature stays at 35.0 °C; a 64 s drive is far too short to heat the pack. The BMS current measurement matches the truth, while the BMS voltage measurement reads about 0.1 V above the terminal truth and the BMS SOC estimate about 0.05 to 0.07 percentage points below it ({fig:F30_battery.png} in {sec:ch04_power/Energy budget}).

In the drive ({fig:F31_drive_internals.png} in {sec:ch03_structure/Structure Signals in the Phase 1 Demonstration}) the motor speeds follow the DRV_CMD references and reach 2168 rpm in the 1.2 m/s segment, which corresponds to 1.21 m/s at the track through the 24:1 gearbox and the 0.128 m sprocket. The applied motor torques stay between -5.3 and 4.8 N m, far inside the 16 N m limit. The steady track slip is about ±11 % in the arcs and ±28 % in the pivot turn (short spikes of up to about ±60 % occur at the drive-off and at the start of the pivot turn), and the winding temperatures rise from 45.0 to about 46.2 °C.
Slope (S2)

S2 (`scn_S2_slope.m`) is the heaviest Phase 1 case. The `slope_test` world has a 20° ramp along +x from x = 10 m to 30 m with 3 m fillets. The robot carries the sprayer with a full tank (609 kg). The throttle commands 0.8 m/s from x = 0 at 4 s and is released so that the robot stops near mid-ramp. It holds there for 30 s, then drives on to the plateau; the run ends at 84 s. This is the first evaluation of S2 with a moving robot: before the fix pass the robot could not move.

blocks.caption: S2 slope (re-run 2026-10-23 20:29): speed against the RC command, body pitch with the MCU tilt estimate and the 22° TILT_WARN threshold, motor torques against the MCU torque limit, and the position with the stop and 30 s hold at x = 18.9 m.

blocks.text: {tab:tab_s2_crit} lists the criteria. The mechanical and electrical loads are well inside their limits: 221.5 N m gearbox peak against 380 N m, 59.6 A pack peak against 150 A, 3.9 K winding rise, and 0.023 m roll-back during the hold. The three failures are connected:

items: **Pitch (T-INT-04).** The mean body pitch on the ramp is -0.388 rad, 0.039 rad (2.2°) steeper than the -0.349 rad ramp. The structure bench T03 found 0.024 rad of contact-compliance pitch on the static 20° ramp, accepted as a spec deviation ({sec:ch03_structure/Verification (Build Task T03)}). The rest of the offset, under traction load with the full sprayer, has not been analysed [TBD - structure domain, T03].

**Tilt warning (D47).** The MCU tilt estimate (`fw_imu_tilt`) reached 26.3°, above the 22° TILT_WARN threshold (`P.electronics.safety.tilt_warn`), from 19.6 s. TILT_WARN is a class-C fault, so the MCU derated the motor torque limit by 0.5, from 16 to 8 N m. TILT_STOP (28°) was not reached, nothing tripped and the climb continued. Two effects add up. First, the true pitch itself reached 23.7°, so a perfect estimator would also have raised TILT_WARN: the 2° between the 20° design slope and the threshold does not cover the compliance and dynamic pitch. Second, the estimate reads about 2° more nose-up than the truth, already on the flat approach before the ramp ({fig:F32_s2_slope.png}). The cause of this bias has not been analysed [TBD - electronics/sensors: fw_imu_tilt bias].

**Ramp speed.** The MCU closes the speed loop on the track belt speed, which held 0.800 m/s on the ramp. The mean ground speed over the same steady moving phases was 0.744 m/s, which is 7.0 % longitudinal slip (1 - 0.744/0.800). The T03 structure bench measured 7.18 % slip for 609 kg climbing a 20° farm-soil ramp at 0.5 m/s (analytic 6.8 ± 1.5 %), so this slip is expected physics, not a defect. A 0.75 m/s limit at a 0.8 m/s command allows only 6.25 % slip.

blocks.text: The derate left little torque reserve: on the ramp the motor torques run close to the derated 8 N m limit ({fig:F32_s2_slope.png}). Items 2 and 3 need a decision, not only a model change: a TILT_WARN threshold with margin above the design slope or a criterion that accepts the warning, and a realistic slip allowance or a belt-speed criterion [TBD - electronics and integration owners].
RC failsafe and corrupted frames (S6)

All S6 variants (`scn_S6_rc_failsafe.m`) drive in MANUAL at 1.0 m/s on the flat test field (transmitter on at 0.5 s, arm at 2 s, throttle at 4 s) and inject an RC fault ({tab:tab_s6_var}). A lost or failed link is a class-B fault: the MCU makes a controlled stop (CTRL_STOP, constant deceleration 1.0 m/s²), changes to STANDBY at standstill and moves again only after the arm switch has been cycled.

Since the decoder fix the scenario script splits it into two cases: at 1 % the decoder must ride through the errors (S6c), and at 5 % the gaps between valid frames exceed the 0.10 s RC timeout, so link loss and a controlled stop are the correct reaction (S6d).

blocks.text: **Link loss and silent line (S6a, S6b).** {tab:tab_s6ab_crit} gives the criteria of both variants. The MCU enters CTRL_STOP 0.12 s (S6a) and 0.09 s (S6b) after the loss onset, inside the 0.13 s D37 budget. The robot is at standstill 1.1 s after detection, never enters ESTOP, and stays still when the link returns at 25 s with the throttle held. It drives again at 0.993 m/s only after the arm switch has been cycled at 29 and 30 s.

**The one failure, deceleration.** The 100 ms moving-average deceleration peaks at 1.15 m/s² against the 1.05 m/s² limit, while the mean 90 % to 10 % deceleration is 1.02 m/s², close to the 1.0 m/s² class-B profile. The vehicle follows the profile on average but exceeds it by about 15 % for a short time. Both variants give the same peak, so the cause lies in the execution of the stop profile, not in the fault detection. By D33 neither the ESC setpoint ramp (2.24 m/s²) nor its QUICK_STOP (2.0 m/s²) limits this stop, so the excess arises between the MCU shaper output and the vehicle motion [TBD - electronics/drive: analyse the stop transient of the MCU shaper and the ESC speed loop].

**Corrupted frames (S6c, S6d).** {tab:tab_s6cd_crit} gives the criteria and {fig:F28_s6_failsafe.png} the frame counts, MCU mode, link status and speed of both runs. At 1 % byte errors the decoder accepts 788 frames and rejects 302 (28 %). Every accepted frame decodes without a channel glitch, and the RC frame age peaks at 92 ms, below the 0.10 s timeout, so the robot continues in MANUAL at 0.993 m/s. The 8 ms margin is small: a slightly higher error rate would trigger the link-loss stop. At 5 % the decoder rejects 937 of 1155 frames (81 %). RC_LINK_LOST then leads to CTRL_STOP in the same 10 ms sample, the robot stops and stays in STANDBY, and no ESTOP occurs. Before the fix pass the decoder passed corrupted bytes to the MCU as valid frames (STATUS section 6, item 8). `sbus_frame_sync.m` now rejects a frame that overlaps a UART error, has a byte after its footer, or carries a channel outside 172..1811.
Emergency stop (S8)
Both S8 variants (`scn_S8_estop.m`) drive in MANUAL at 1.2 m/s and trigger an E-stop at 10 s. {tab:tab_s8_crit} gives the criteria of both variants.

items: **S8a, front hardware E-stop.** The button is pressed from 10 to 15 s (throttle held until 16 s), the reset button is pressed from 17.0 to 17.3 s, and the arm switch is cycled at 19 and 20 s with the sticks neutral; throttle again at 21 s. This path is hardware: the dual-channel loop opens the safety relay, which activates STO on both ESCs (torque off, spring brakes engage) and, after 1.5 s, removes the K1/K2 coil supply. The MCU only sees the E-stop through a digital input.

**S8b, remote E-stop (CH12).** The latching switch on the transmitter is thrown from 10 to 15 s. This path is firmware: the MCU enters ESTOP, stops with the 2.0 m/s² constant-deceleration profile and keeps ESTOP latched after the switch returns to RUN.

blocks.text: **Hardware E-stop (S8a).** STO acts 15 ms after the plant-side button edge, and the MCU sets the HW_ESTOP fault bit 8 ms after the DI change. With torque off and the spring brakes engaged, the robot stops in 0.213 m from 1.19 m/s, a mean deceleration of about 3.3 m/s². The chassis rocks briefly after the hard stop ({fig:F29_s8_estop.png}), so the no-restart window starts 2 s after ESTOP entry. Safety_HV_OK opens 1.5 s after the E-stop through the delayed relay contacts. After the reset at 17 s the relay closes and the MCU changes from ESTOP to STANDBY; HV_Ready returns about 0.5 s later. The MCU returns to MANUAL only on the re-arm at 20 s. Before the fix pass the robot did not restart, because the ESCs latched an undervoltage fault after K1 opened (STATUS section 6, item 9); that fault now latches only while the power stage is enabled.

**Remote E-stop (S8b).** The MCU enters ESTOP 0.07 s after the switch, within the 92 ms worst-case latency of D33, and the robot stops in 0.592 m (D33 replay 0.62 m, limit 0.70 m). ESTOP stays latched after CH12 returns to RUN. The one failure is the mean deceleration of 2.119 m/s², 0.9 % above the 2.1 m/s² upper bound; the peak of 2.27 m/s² is inside its 2.4 m/s² limit. This is the same pattern as in S6a and S6b: the vehicle decelerates slightly harder than the MCU profile. The deviation shortens the stop distance, but the criterion bounds the profile itself, so it remains a failure until the stop transient is understood (same TBD as S6).

Assessment and next steps

Phase 1 is demonstrated: the complete chain from the transmitter to the tracks works end to end, the D37 latency budgets are met (28 ms against 30 ms, 50 ms against 65 ms), both E-stop paths and both RC-loss modes stop the robot within their latency, standstill and stop-distance limits without misusing ESTOP (the deceleration-profile limits of S6a, S6b and S8b are exceeded slightly, see below), and the robot moves again only after the required re-arm (S6a, S6b) or reset and re-arm (S8a). The open failures are the deceleration deviations of the stop profiles (short peaks in S6a and S6b, a 0.9 % high mean in S8b) and the slope case S2, where the TILT_WARN threshold and the speed criterion leave too little room for the physical pitch and slip. Recommended next steps:

items: Re-run `tScenarios` and the full regression in a fresh MATLAB session, and update the stale tests (STATUS item 17).
Analyse the stop transient behind the S6a, S6b and S8b deceleration peaks.
Decide the S2 tilt threshold and speed criterion, and find the source of the 2° tilt-estimate bias.
